title: Convergent invocation surface: async adapters + typed tool contracts (TS/Python/Go)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define and implement a single, convergent invocation surface that lets TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs present a consistent streaming + tool-calling + structured-output developer experience while remaining backward compatible. This ticket defines adapter interfaces (async iterators, framed event envelopes), a minimal typed tool contract schema, and a set of runnable examples for each language. The focus is on clarity for library authors and minimal runtime changes for customers using existing SDK versions.
background: Multiple language SDKs currently expose slightly different streaming primitives and tool-call shapes which creates confusion for multi-language client teams and makes cross-lang examples fragile. We need an interoperability layer that preserves streaming semantics (progressive tokens + structured events), supports tool/function calling with typed input/output, and can be progressively adopted via shims in older SDK releases.
acceptance_criteria: A1: All three SDKs (TS/Python/Go) provide a documented 'InvokeStream' API that yields a stable event envelope with fields: type, value, seq, and optional tool_call metadata.
A2: Examples show how to implement a tool handler that receives a typed JSON payload and returns either a terminal result or stream of progress events in each language.
A3: Backwards compatibility: existing streaming consumers using the previous SDK streaming iterator continue to work with a compatibility shim for at least one minor release.
A4: End-to-end tests validate structured-schema enforcement for tool inputs and outputs (JSON Schema v2020-12) and fail fast on mismatch.
A5: Performance regression: no more than 5% additional median latency on small-token streaming workloads (<= 64 tokens) in CI benchmarks when the shim is enabled.
A6: Documentation and snippet gallery published in docs/sdk/interop with copy-paste examples for each language.
A7: Security review for typed tool contract (injection/validation edge cases) completed if enabled by default in the SDK.
plan: 1) API design: finalize event envelope and tool contract schema (this ticket).
2) TS SDK: implement InvokeStream + compat shim, add unit tests and examples.
3) Python SDK: implement async generator InvokeStream, validation hook, examples.
4) Go SDK: implement channel-based stream adapter and typed tool handler.
5) E2E tests: cross-lang harness that runs the same prompt and asserts structured events.
6) Docs: add migration guide and cookbook snippets.
7) Rollout: ship compat shim in minor release, enable default in next major after 2-week opt-in period.
risks: R1: Schema validation on hot paths could add CPU overhead; mitigated by opt-in validation and fast path bypass.
R2: Behavioral mismatch in Go channel semantics vs async iterators could confuse patterns; solution: explicit semantic mapping documented.
R3: Tool contract errors may leak internal data if not sanitized; require sanitizer hooks in SDK.
R4: Customers using custom streaming parsers may need migration guidance.
